en: Most modern
AI models that power Claude or Microsoft
Copilot and so on are visual language
models, but technically they are multimodal
models, which means
they are AI models that are able to
understand and combine and also reason about
different kinds of inputs, which means text
and images or video, for example, but that
they can also generate information in more
than one modality. So they can generate
text, but they can also generate images or
audio or video. Now, it depends on the model
that you're using. For example, the Claude
models can understand images. They are
visual language models, but they can't
output images, at least at the point of time
where I'm recording this. But some models
like the ChatGPT models, they can actually
do multiple things. Now, technically behind
the scenes, different kinds of models are
simply being combined there, but still
you're dealing with an AI assistant, for
example, that is capable of understanding
images and text and that's able to generate
images and text.
So therefore, it's also important to
understand that multimodality is not so much
about one single model, but also about the
combination of AI models in some AI
software. Such that the software is able to
do more than just understand or output text.
